SANDBACH UNITED MATCHDAY PREVIEW - WEEKEND 22-23 AUGUST 2026

This weekend sees Sandbach travel to take on New Mills at Church Lane on Saturday, looking to build on last weekend's impressive 1-0 victory against Stafford Town. The Bach have made an excellent start to their league campaign with two wins from three, sitting joint second in the table on 6 points.

New Mills will present a stern test, however. The Millers have shown their attacking prowess this season and bounced back impressively from a heavy 5-0 defeat at Stafford in midweek with a 2-1 victory over Allscott Heath. They're currently on 6 points as well, meaning this is very much a fixture between two sides capable of mounting a serious title challenge.

Sandbach's defensive solidity has been key to their success so far. A clean sheet against Stafford, combined with the earlier wins, suggests manager's setup is working well. The Bach have also shown character in difficult moments - their midweek defeat at Foley Meir (3-2) demonstrated they can score goals when needed, even if they ultimately fell short.

Key talking points for this fixture: both sides are among the pacesetters in Division One South. Wolverhampton Casuals sit top with three wins from three, but there's everything to play for in the chase behind them. A win for Sandbach would take them to 9 points and maintain their challenge. For New Mills, victory would put them in a similar position.

The Bach should take confidence from their recent form, particularly the defensive displays. However, New Mills at home will be a different proposition than facing Stafford last week. Luc Ferry impressed for the Millers last Saturday and they'll be keen to assert themselves on their own pitch.

Robbie Hatton's continued performances have been crucial for Sandbach's success. His leadership and finishing ability could be the difference in what promises to be a competitive encounter. Manager will likely instruct the team to be defensively disciplined while looking to exploit opportunities on the break.

This is exactly the type of fixture that can define a season. Both teams are capable, both are starting well, and bragging rights over a local rival often carry extra significance. Sandbach's experience from last week's defeat at Foley should serve them well - they know they can compete at this level and create chances. If they can replicate their defensive performance from the Stafford match while adding clinical finishing, the three points are well within reach.
